Smith Center]] | champion = |tourney = |tourney_result = }} {{2022–23 ACC men's basketball standings}} The '''2022–23 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]] during the [[2022–23 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The team was led by [[Hubert Davis]], who was in his second year as UNC's head coach. The Tar Heels played their home games at the [[Dean Smith Center]] in [[Chapel Hill, North Carolina|Chapel Hill]], as members of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]]. The Tar Heels, coming off a National Runner-up in the [[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2022 NCAA tournament]], were ranked #1 in the Preseason [[AP poll]], and failed to live up to the lofty expectations the ranking entailed. The team struggled offensively all season, finishing the season with the second-worst 3-point-percentage in program history. The 2022-23 Tar Heels went 1-9 in NET quad 1 games (their only Q1 victory being a home win against #6 [[2022–23 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|Virginia]]).{{cite web|url=https://www.dailytarheel.com/article/2023/02/unc-basketball-virginia-win-3-point-shooting-quad-one-win-pete-nance|title=UNC men's basketball earns first Quad One win of season in 71-63 victory over No. 6 Virginia|last=Nelson|first=Hunter|publisher=Daily Tar Heel|date=February 25, 2023|access-date=March 13, 2023}} They finished the season 20–13 overall and 11–9 in [[2022–23 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]], earning the 7 seed in the [[2023 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC Tournament]]. On Selection Sunday, the Tar Heels were not picked to be a part of the field for the [[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2023 NCAA Tournament]], and were one of the first four teams left out by the selection committee. By narrowly missing out on a spot in the tournament, the Tar Heels became the first preseason #1-ranked team to miss the tournament since the field expanded to 64 teams in 1985.{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/north-carolina-declines-nit-invite-after-becoming-first-preseason-no-1-team-to-miss-ncaa-tournament/|title=North Carolina declines NIT invite after becoming first preseason No. 1 team to miss NCAA Tournament|last=Cobb|first=David|website=cbssports.com|publisher=CBS Sports|date=March 12, 2023|access-date=March 13, 2023}} Following the missed bid, coach Hubert Davis announced via statement that the team would decline an invite to the [[2023 National Invitation Tournament|2023 NIT]], ending their season. ==Previous season== In [[Hubert Davis]]' first year at the helm, the Tar Heels got off to a rocky start, with blowout losses to [[2021–22 Tennessee Volunteers basketball team|Tennessee]], [[2021–22 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky]], [[2021–22 Miami Hurricanes men's basketball team|Miami]], [[2021–22 Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball team|Wake Forest]], and [[2021–22 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]] (at home). The Tar Heels rounded into form in the latter half of conference play, finishing with a 15–5 record in conference play. The Tar Heels capped the regular season with an upset win over the Blue Devils at Cameron Indoor Stadium in [[Mike Krzyzewski]]'s final home game.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/game/_/gameId/401369869|title=North Carolina vs. Duke - Game Summary - March 5, 2022|website=ESPN|access-date=April 6, 2022}} The Tar Heels earned the No. 3 seed and a double-bye in the [[2022 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]].{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/Article/ACC-Tournament-2022-Bracket-schedule-scores-how-to-watch-183813095/|title=ACC Tournament 2022: Bracket, schedule, scores, how to watch|first=Chance|last=Linton|website=247Sports.com|date=March 12, 2022|access-date=April 6, 2022}} They defeated [[2021–22 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|Virginia]] in the quarterfinals before losing to eventual champions [[2021–22 Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball team|Virginia Tech]] in the semifinals. The Tar Heels earned the No. 8 seed in the East Region of the 2022 [[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2022/sports/ncaabasketball/mens-ncaa-bracket-march-madness.html|title=2022 N.C.A.A. Men’s Tournament Bracket and Results|website=The New York Times|access-date=April 6, 2022}} In the tournament, they beat [[2021–22 Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball team|Marquette]] and upset No. 1 seed in [[2021–22 Baylor Bears men's basketball team|Baylor]] to earn North Carolina's 35th Sweet Sixteen appearance of all time. The Tar Heels upset No. 4 seed [[2021–22 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|UCLA]] and beat "Cinderella" team [[2021–22 Saint Peter's Peacocks basketball team|Saint Peter's]] in the Elite Eight. The Tar Heels earned a record 21st Final Four appearance, where they beat the Blue Devils in the first-ever NCAA Tournament matchup between the rival schools, 81–77, before falling 69–72 against Kansas in the [[2022 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Championship Game|National Championship]] game. Starters [[Brady Manek]], [[Armando Bacot]], [[Caleb Love]], [[R. J. Davis]], and [[Leaky Black]] earned the nickname "The Iron 5" for their togetherness and strong play as a unit throughout the season, and for the fact they played a large amount of the team's minutes throughout the campaign. Against Duke in Durham, Bacot, Love, Davis, and Manek each scored twenty-plus points in a game, the first time four players went for twenty or more in one game in Carolina basketball history. Head coach Davis became only the second person in history to take the same school to the Final Four as both a player and a coach, joining Kansas' [[Dick Harp]]. Davis also became the 10th first-year head coach in history to take his team to the Final Four.{{cite web|url=https://www.tarheelblog.com/2022/3/30/22999147/unc-tar-heels-basketball-hubert-davis-coach-final-four-first-season|title=UNC Basketball: Hubert Davis joins an exclusive group of coaches|first=Matt|last=Ferenchick|website=Tar Heel Blog|date=March 30, 2022|access-date=April 6, 2022}} ==Offseason== After the conclusion of the 2021–22 season, Anthony Harris and [[Dawson Garcia]] entered the transfer portal. Garcia announced he would transfer to Minnesota to be closer with family in the wake of the family issues that forced him to miss the latter half of the previous season.{{cite web|url=https://www.startribune.com/dawson-garcia-minnesota-gophers-transfer-north-carolina-marquette/600165837/|title=Dawson Garcia commits to Gophers, wants to be part of 'getting Minnesota basketball back'|first=Marcus|last=Fuller|date=April 19, 2022|website=Star Tribune|access-date=April 19, 2022}} Brady Manek also left the team, as the previous season was his final year of collegiate eligibility. Manek had taken advantage of the extra year given out by the NCAA in response to COVID-19 to play for the Tar Heels in 2021–22. Harris committed to transfer to [[Rhode Island Rams men's basketball|Rhode Island]] in May, but was unable to enroll at URI due to reported academic issues.{{cite web|url=https://www.providencejournal.com/story/sports/2022/09/12/uri-mens-basketball-anthony-harris-north-carolina-transfer-delayed-enrollment-at-uri/8058067001/|title= Academic woes will delay UNC transfer Anthony Harris' enrollment at URI|first=Bill|last=Koch|website=The Providence Journal|date=September 12, 2022|access-date=September 26, 2022}} Guard Kerwin Walton also announced plans to transfer on May 1, 2022, the last day to enter the portal and maintain eligibility for the following season.{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/north-carolina/Article/UNC-Basketball-Kerwin-Walton-Enters-Transfer-Portal-187029341/|title=BREAKING: UNC's Kerwin Walton Enters Transfer Portal|first=Greg|last=Barnes|website=Inside Carolina|date=May 1, 2022|access-date=May 1, 2022}} After speculation that he would turn pro and enter the [[2022 NBA draft]], Armando Bacot confirmed his return in a video for the 2022–23 season on April 13, 2022.{{Cite web |title=Carolina Basketball on Twitter |url=https://twitter.com/unc_basketball/status/1514273773662351367 |access-date=2022-04-13 |website=Twitter |language=en}} A few days later, Leaky Black, R.
